name: Flagger STOP/SLOW paddle
spec: hand-held paddle on a staff: red octagon face with white legend STOP
meaning: When the flagger shows STOP, stop and wait; SLOW means proceed slowly.

snippets.back: Flaggers commonly wear orange and use red flags or stop-and-slow paddles to direct drivers.
Flaggers communicate using signals, stop-or-slow paddles, highly visible flags, and sometimes other signs.

Orange diamond or square work boards warn of crews, slow detours, crawling machines and shifting pavement, detour boards open the backup path, and flaggers in bright vests with paddles and red flags rule the zone absolutely.
STOP and SLOW paddles used by trained flaggers can control movement through a work zone.
Temporary signals, police or certified flaggers with stop slash slow paddles may control stopped work-zone traffic.
Flagpersons stop, slow or guide traffic through work zones, wear orange vests, shirts or jackets, and direct traffic with red flags or stop and slow paddles.
Flaggers with stop-or-slow paddles direct work traffic and must be obeyed; they wear fluorescent yellow-green or orange and mostly use paddle signs, with red flags only at times.
When a flagger uses a sign paddle, stop for the STOP side and proceed slowly for the SLOW side.
